hypothesis: A comparison harness with an analytic tolerance policy separates legitimate reduction-order and precision differences from faults: once the fault-free candidate is within the policy, every fault larger than twice the tolerance is detected, detection switches at about the tolerance, and faults up to about the bound escape as often as the fault-size distribution predicts. On the common Gaussian VI workload, whose reductions have a fixed order, T148's policy prescribes a bitwise comparison: it accepts a second implementation of the declared order and flags a build that contracts multiply-adds, and on a GPU host it compares the gaussian_vi PTX kernel's outputs with the CPU reference.
input_data: orders: sequential, pairwise tree, 32-lane blocked (sequential lanes then tree); precisions float64 and float32
exact dot products by TwoProduct + math.fsum
all 131072 single dropped products per policy, judged by compare_outputs

the common Gaussian VI workload (examples/energy-accuracy/problem.json, K = 38): the float64 NumPy reference, a scalar evaluation of the same order, two exact fused multiply-add contractions, and on a GPU host the gaussian_vi PTX kernel's outputs for every replica
mathematical_model: For a sum of terms each passing through k roundings, |computed - exact| <= gamma_k * sum|a_j x_j| with gamma_k = k u/(1 - k u), u = 2^-53 (float64) or 2^-24 (float32, inputs rounded). The policy tolerance for two outputs is the sum of their bounds, so the fault-free candidate satisfies |c - r| <= tol; bitwise mode compares bit patterns. A dropped term p gives |c - p - r| >= |p| - tol, so |p| > 2 tol is detected without knowing c - r; with m = max |c - r|/tol, detection switches inside (1 +/- m) tol. With a_ij uniform on [-1, 1), P(|a_ij x_j| <= tol_i) = min(1, tol_i/|x_j|), whose sum over faults predicts the miss count.
numerical_result: 123/128 rows flagged by the bitwise policy between float64 orders (0 for a copy of the reference); max difference/bound 0.00173; float32 violates the float64 policy on 128 rows and stays at 0.00874 of its own bound; faults above twice the tolerance left undetected: 0/131072 (float64 policy), 0/129813 (float32 policy); single dropped products undetected: 0/131072 (float64), 708/131072 (float32, predicted 665.3 +/- 22.5; largest missed |a_j x_j| 0.000589 against row tolerance 0.000594; 1 missed above the row bound, ratio 1.00016).
